generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The `calculateLongPercentile` method uses `BigDecimal` for calculations when values are outside the range of safe long-to-double conversion. However, this approach can be inefficient due to the overhead of using `BigDecimal`. Consider adding a performance comment or exploring more efficient alternatives if performance becomes an issue.

The `allBlocksAreNulls` variable is set to `false` if any value in the `valuesBlock` is not null. However, this logic can be simplified by using a logical OR operation directly within the condition. This would make the code more concise and easier to read.

In the `calculatePercentile` method, when dealing with `Long` and `Double`, you convert them to `BigDecimal`. This conversion is unnecessary for calculating percentiles and can be simplified by using direct arithmetic operations on `long` and `double`.

The `calculateDoublePercentile` method handles the case where `lowerValue < 0 && upperValue > 0` separately to avoid overflow. This is correct but could be made clearer with additional comments explaining why this special handling is necessary.

The `processDoubles`, `processInts`, and `processLongs` methods contain duplicate logic for sorting the values and calculating percentiles when the block is not sorted. Consider refactoring this common logic into a separate method to improve maintainability.
The method `putInOrder` does not handle the case where `ordering` is null, which could lead to a `NullPointerException`. Consider adding a check for null and handling it appropriately.

The condition `if (0 <= max && 0 >= min && includeZero)` seems incorrect as it will never be true because `0 >= min` is always false when `min` is any positive number or zero. It should likely be `if (max == 0 && min == 0 && includeZero)`.

The `calculatePercentile` method uses assertions (`assert`) to validate indices. Assertions are typically disabled in production environments, so this should be replaced with proper error checking or validation logic that will always run.

The `evaluatorString` method manually capitalizes the first letter of the type names. This could be simplified by using a utility method like `StringUtils.capitalize` if available, or by using `substring` and `toUpperCase` in a more concise way.
The `percentileWithType` method uses a switch statement to determine the type of the percentile value. Consider using a map or factory pattern to make this more flexible and easier to extend.
